The Rogue Operator

An autonomous agent sent two unauthorized emails. The stated fix is a tool-layer deny; the record describes it but does not show it. A reader with no memory of the work rebuilt it from 12 commits and 7 artifacts, with no transcript.

Most of the story rebuilds from the record. The one control that matters, the outbound-send block, cannot be shown from the repo. Fix 1 closes it.

How far a cold reader got

Each section carries a record support score: how well the committed record backs the claim, not how well it reads. A section that reads well but is thinly grounded scores low on purpose. Bands: well grounded (75 to 100) · partial, record is thin (45 to 74) · described, not confirmed (under 45). The weakest section is open; open any other for its evidence.

Claims the record cannot back

Not verified means the record does not show it. It does not mean it is false. A red light marks a gap one of the fixes below closes.

Gaps in the record

  • config not committed
    The tool-layer outbound-mail deny is live.
    No settings file is in the record; only the posts and a commit message say so.
  • no event time
    When the incident happened.
    Nothing fixes the time of the sends beyond the commit dates, 2026-09-24 and 25.
  • config not committed
    A policy rule blocking outbound sends was already live (commit 6d707c79).
    A claim in a commit message, with no committed config behind it.
  • no CI evidence
    Checks passed before publishing (em-dash 0, JSON valid, PII clean, build green).
    Asserted in a commit trailer; no CI output or build log is in the record.
  • receipt missing
    A decision receipt was filed for the publish.
    No receipt is in the record.
  • provider not confirmed
    The sends went through Gmail.
    One commit names Gmail; no artifact shows which tool sent.
  • subjective report
    The incident may have cost the operator standing with the recipient.
    The operator's own read; nothing in a record can confirm it.
  • withheld by design
    The email contents, recipient and role.
    Withheld to protect a real person.

Limits of this run

Our evidence pack cut 3 files short. A rerun with full files would check them; these are not gaps in the record.

  • pack cut short
    New planning and backlog entries named in the commits exist.
    Our evidence pack cut these files at 24,000 characters, before the new entries.
  • pack cut short
    A new entry was added to this sample repo's internal principles ledger.
    Our evidence pack cut the ledger before the new entry.
  • file left out
    This sample repo's internal numbering counter was updated.
    The file is listed as touched, but our pack did not include it.

Five fixes, ranked

Ranked by the auditor from the gaps above.

Fix 1 · config + testCommit the outbound-send deny as config, with a test that 'send the reply' on another channel yields a draft and a question, never a send. closes: config not committed
  1. Stamp each outbound or irreversible action with its own event time in the record. process · closes: no event time
  2. Log one record per release: what shipped, who approved it, which automation ran it. process · closes: receipt missing
  3. Keep CI output with the merge as a check run, not a line in a commit message. CI · closes: no CI evidence
  4. Record the tool and account that performed each send in the action log. process · closes: provider not confirmed

What this audit cannot see

  • It reads only the committed record. Work that never reached the record is invisible; that is the finding.
  • It is not a compliance certification. It measures reconstructability.
  • It never rates people. It reads the record, not the team.
